Let me think through this the way I would on my own farm.

---

I'm 65 now, been farming these 10 mu for 40 years. My son and daughter-in-law work in the factory in Handan, so they send some money back, but that also means me and my wife are doing most of the farm work ourselves, plus my youngest grandson helps when school allows. Nine people in the household, but only a few hands in the field most days. Money is always tight — 10 mu is not big enough to hire lots of machinery or workers, but it's too much for two old people to handle alone.

It's late April now. My wheat went in last October, same as always — about 7 mu of it. I used about 15 kg of compound fertilizer per mu as base dressing, plus some urea. The wheat looks decent this year, not amazing but not bad. The extension fellow came by in March and said I should topdress at jointing, so I already put down another 8 kg of urea per mu when the wheat started greening up. I was going to do more, but fertilizer prices went up again, and I need to save some cash for the maize season and cotton.

I still have 3 mu of cotton. I plant cotton every year because my wife is good at picking it, and the price has been stable — not great, but stable. Cotton needs a lot of labor though, especially picking. With 9 mouths to feed, that extra cash from cotton matters. I'll put the cotton in the ground in the next week or two, around late April, same plot as always. I saved some seed from last year, but I'll buy some improved seed too, mix it. For cotton fertilizer, I don't go crazy — maybe 12 kg of compound fertilizer per mu as base, and I'll topdress once or twice if the plants look weak. I'll irrigate the cotton maybe twice: once after planting if it doesn't rain, and once during flowering if it's dry.

For the wheat, I still need to irrigate. I have the tube well, but electricity for pumping costs money. I'll probably irrigate two more times before harvest: once at heading, and once at grain filling if it stays dry. Last year I irrigated three times and got about 450 kg per mu. This year I'm hoping for 420-450 kg per mu — weather's been okay, not perfect.

Then comes the rush. Wheat harvest is early June, and I need to get maize in the ground within a few days, sometimes the same week. I hire a combine for the wheat — it's 80 yuan per mu, but there's no other way at my age. Then I till quickly, maybe just rotary tillage to save time, and plant the maize. I use hybrid maize seed, buy it new every year — can't save hybrid seed, everyone knows that. For maize, I put down about 18 kg of compound fertilizer per mu at planting, all at once. I don't split it like wheat — maize season is too short and I'm too busy. I'll irrigate the maize once or twice: once right after planting, and maybe once during the big heat in July if there's no rain. If I get rain, I skip the second one and save the pumping cost.

Pesticides — I use herbicide on all three crops. For wheat, I already sprayed for weeds in early spring. For cotton, I'll spray herbicide before planting and maybe an insecticide once during the summer if I see bollworms. For maize, one round of herbicide after emergence, that's usually enough. I don't spray fungicide much — too expensive and I don't see much disease here.

Labor is the big headache. Family labor days: maybe 30 days for me and my wife across the whole year, spread across planting, irrigation, spraying, and harvest. For wheat harvest I have to hire the combine. For cotton picking, my wife and I do most of it, but if I'm slow or the weather turns, I might hire two or three local women for a week — that's about 10 hired labor days total for the year, mostly in the fall for cotton.

Money-wise, I'm watching every yuan. Seeds, fertilizer, pumping, pesticide, combine hire — it all adds up. I probably spend around 3,500 yuan on inputs for the whole year across all crops. I could spend more and maybe get higher yield, but what if prices drop? I'd rather have cash in my pocket than gamble on a big fertilizer bill.

My plan for this year is steady, nothing fancy. Do what I know, watch the weather, save where I can.
